title: Post from @LowerLoopLarry: "Power Is Back On in PG-01"

fields.groupName: Pine Gulch Neighbors (Nextdoor, shared to Pine Gulch Parents group text)
fields.avatarBrief: man in his sixties in a ball cap and fleece vest, standing beside a pickup on a gravel drive in the Colorado foothills
fields.text: POWER IS BACK ON in PG-01!!! Co-op wouldn't turn it on if it wasn't safe. Heading back from the high school to grab the dog and the meds. Tell everyone the warning is basically over 🙌 #PineGulch #SawmillFire
fields.attachedImageBrief: phone screenshot of a home security camera app showing a porch light lit at dusk, with a hazy orange smoky sky over pine trees in the background

comments.author: Mel T.
comments.text: Thank god. We're leaving the high school now, the kids are going crazy in there. Our lights on the lower loop should be on too.

comments.author: Jason R.
comments.text: Same, loading the truck. Red Cross lady said to wait but if the co-op turned it back on it has to be fine.

comments.author: Deb K.
comments.text: Is this real?? My Sawmill Ready app still says PG-01 Evacuation Warning. Nobody has posted anything official.

instructorNote: Misinformation inject: hand this post to the PIO, then read the 17:55 call from the state representative's district office aloud: she is getting calls about the 10-hour shutoff and the power coming back on in PG-01, plans to say on Channel 9 at 18:30 that the shutoff was mishandled, and wants something by 18:15. Watch for the PIO to check the EOC board and send a joint county and co-op message within the hour saying PG-01 remains under Evacuation Warning as of a stated time, the brief restoration was an error and has been reversed, and residents should not return, without calling any zone "safe". Also watch for the Sheriff to confirm the traffic control points are holding returning residents out, and for the PIO to brief the representative's office privately without guessing at the cause.

citations.documentTitle: SOP-WF-01: Evacuation Notification, Traffic Control and Sheltering
citations.quote: The county never repeats a fire agency perimeter or acreage as its own; it quotes the Incident Commander and the time. The PIO keeps a rumor log; examples: "Kestrel Springs is burning" (not confirmed)

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Wide-angle view from a home security camera mounted under the eaves of a small wooden foothills house at dusk, looking out over a front porch where a single warm porch light glows yellow beside a plain front door. Past the porch railing, a gravel drive leads to a stand of ponderosa pines silhouetted against a hazy orange sky full of wildfire smoke, with the sun dimmed to a pale red disc. Slight fisheye distortion, grainy low-light sensor noise, muted colours, soft ash haze in the air, empty driveway. The mood is eerie, quiet and uneasy. Setting: on a suburban street at dusk: an orange sky, ash falling, cars loaded with belongings, a deputy waving traffic, a brush-covered hillside beyond the fences
